basics.name: Ningdong Wang
basics.label: Researcher and programmer
basics.summary: Researcher and programmer working on scientific software and AI systems, including GPU-accelerated simulation, learned models, and agents for technical workflows. Physics PhD student at Cornell University.

experience.name: Cornell University
experience.summary: Implemented cathode space-charge tracking in Bmad and studied RF cavity coupler effects on beam quality. Develop GPU-accelerated simulation tools in Julia and machine learning surrogates for beam dynamics and electric-field prediction. Develop MCP-connected agents for accelerator simulations and control systems, with evaluations of correctness and reliability on operational tasks. Contribute to Osprey, a multi-institution framework for agentic AI in accelerator control systems. Supervised by Georg Hoffstaetter.

experience.name: Shizuku AI
experience.summary: Built a text-to-speech data pipeline that generated 25,000 hours of training audio. Optimized TTS inference, reducing time to first audio from 600 ms to 180 ms. Developed a real-time multimodal agent harness integrating audio, vision, audience comments, tool calls, and speech output.

experience.name: Brookhaven National Laboratory
experience.summary: Modeled space charge and collective effects for Electron-Ion Collider cooling systems. Optimized the Strong Hadron Cooler injector and merger in Bmad and Xopt, reducing simulated normalized transverse emittance by 62% and RMS energy spread by 85% relative to the original configuration.

experience.name: Argonne National Laboratory
experience.summary: Modeled and optimized a spin-rotator solenoid array for the SuperKEKB electron storage ring. Supervised by Uli Wienands.

experience.name: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign
experience.summary: Studied electron spin polarization in quantum point contacts and its effect on conductance. Supervised by Jean-Pierre Leburton.

publications.name: Electron Ion Collider Strong Hadron Cooling design Summary
Multi-objective optimization of Strong Hadron Cooler Energy Recovery Linac injector
publications.publisher: Proceedings of the North American Particle Accelerator Conference (NAPAC2025)
publications.summary: The Strong Hadron Cooler (SHC) proposed for the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) requires high-current, low-emittance electron bunches with minimal energy spread. The Energy Recovery Linac (ERL) injector plays a critical role in shaping the beam before acceleration. We present a multi-objective optimization study of the SHC ERL injector and merger using space charge tracking in Bmad and parallel genetic algorithm. The optimized configuration reduces the normalized transverse emittance by 62% and energy spread by 85% from the original configuration.

publications.name: Optimization of cooling distribution of the EIC SHC cooler ERL
publications.publisher: Proceedings of the 15th International Particle Accelerator Conference (IPAC'24)
publications.summary: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) Hadron Storage Ring (HSR) will use strong hadron cooling to maintain the beam brightness and high luminosity during long collision experiments. An Energy Recovery Linac is used to deliver the high-current high-brightness electron beam for cooling. For the best cooling effect, the electron beam requires low emittance, small energy spread, and uniform longitudinal distribution. In this work, we simulate and optimize the longitudinal laser-beam distribution shaping at the photocathode, modeling space charge forces accurately. Machine parameters such as RF cavity phases are optimized in conjunction with the beam distribution using a genetic optimizer. We demonstrate improvement of the cooling distribution in key parameters.

publications.name: EIC cooler injector space charge benchmark
publications.publisher: Proceedings of the 14th International Particle Accelerator Conference (IPAC'23)
publications.summary: In this paper, we present the benchmark results of Bmad space charge tracking on the Electron-Ion Collider cooler injector lattice. Bmad, GPT, and Impact-T are compared in terms of accuracy and performance. We highlight the importance of space charge algorithm and demonstrate that the adaptive step size control improves the performance of Bmad space charge tracking.

publications.name: Cathode Space Charge in Bmad
publications.publisher: Proceedings of the 13th International Particle Accelerator Conference (IPAC'22)
publications.summary: We present an implementation of charged particle tracking with the cathode space charge effect included which is now openly available in the Bmad toolkit for charged particle simulations. Adaptive step size control is incorporated to improve the computational efficiency. We demonstrate its capability with a simulation of a DC gun and compare it with the well-established space charge code Impact-T.
